title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. Earlier pages set up a category with a distinguished class Σ of 'Σ-exact' sequences: an exact structure in Quillen's sense, or a relative homological algebra in the sense of Hochschild and Eilenberg–Moore. Inside it sit additive subcategories P_0 ⊂ P_1 ⊂ P. The previous page noted that kernels exist but are not always Σ-monos, so the general category is not Σ-abelian.

This page restricts to Φ_1 = Q, which is equivalent to the category Q of finite chain complexes of k-modules whose chains L_i, cycles Z_i, boundaries B_i and homology H_i are all free of finite type. The marginal note gives the induced exact structure: Σ_1 = Σ ∩ P_1.

Over a field, or with these freeness conditions, every such complex splits as a finite direct sum of two kinds of elementary pieces:
- the contractible 'discs' C^i (k →id k placed in degrees i, i−1);
- the 'spheres' (k in a single degree). Ψ^0 is the unit/constant object, k in degree 0.
The Φ^i are presumably the normalized chains of the standard i-simplex, i.e. C-type pieces together with Ψ^0. This fits the title (half-simplicial complexes).

Grothendieck identifies the relative projectives and injectives:
- Σ-projectives = the additive subcategory P_0 generated by the C^i and Ψ^0 (equivalently by the Φ^i);
- Σ-injectives = the additive subcategory K generated by the C^i alone. These are the acyclic objects, translated into the 'flasque' language of a coefficient system L_*.

He proposes to study right Σ-injective resolutions K^• of Ψ^0, i.e. 'flasque resolutions K_* of k_*'. These would supply an algebraic model and remarkable computational methods for cohomology with coefficients in k, presumably aiming at functorial cochains carrying multiplicative structure.

He then invokes the comparison theorem of relative homological algebra. If every object embeds by a Σ-mono into a Σ-injective, then any two Σ-injective resolutions are homotopy equivalent, with a unique homotopy class of maps between them. Dually there are enough Σ-projectives, giving the analogous statement for projective resolutions.

The next page continues the plan. It defines derived functors R^iF of additive functors F: Q → B and sets H^i(F) := R^iF(Ψ^0). It identifies these as the derived functors of evaluation F ↦ F(Ψ^0) on the category of Σ-functors P → B, which is shown equivalent to complexes B^•. Under this equivalence evaluation becomes C^• ↦ Z^0 = H^0, so RF(Ψ^0) ≃ F(C^•). This is a representability statement: Ψ^0 has a canonical Σ-injective resolution, and every additive functor's derived functors at Ψ^0 are computed by applying F to it.
errors: Possible tension, depending on Σ (defined on earlier pages, not fully legible here). If Σ-exactness required short exactness on H as well, the embedding Ψ^0 → C^? into a disc would not be a Σ-mono, since homology is not injective, and Ψ^0 could not have a Σ-injective resolution by C^i's. So Σ must be exactness on L, Z, B (or degreewise split), with H governed by the long exact sequence. The page does not make this explicit.

Rest is a standard application of the relative comparison theorem; no mathematical error is visible. The draft is partly crossed out and hesitant, e.g. on whether K together with Ψ^0 gives enough projectives.

ideas.what: Exact structure Σ on a category of finite free chain complexes, with Σ-projectives generated by discs and spheres (Φ^i) and Σ-injectives by discs C^i
ideas.modern_name: Exact category / relative homological algebra (Frobenius-type structure on split complexes)

ideas.what: Uniqueness up to homotopy of relative injective/projective resolutions when there are enough Σ-injectives/projectives
ideas.modern_name: Comparison theorem in relative homological algebra

ideas.what: Σ-injective ('flasque') resolution of the constant object Ψ^0 = k as a source of computational models for cohomology with coefficients in k (presumably for multiplicative structures on cochains of semi-simplicial complexes)
ideas.modern_name: Acyclic-models style canonical cochain resolutions (cf. Sullivan / Cartan simplicial cochain models)

ideas.what: (next page) H^i(F) = R^iF(Ψ^0), identified with derived functors of evaluation on the category of Σ-additive functors, which is equivalent to complexes B^•
ideas.modern_name: Functor homology / derived evaluation, Yoneda-type representability
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gabriel–Zisman; later functor homology (Pirashvili, Franjou et al.)

missed.claim: Programme to obtain canonical Σ-injective ('flasque') resolutions of the constant coefficient k_* on semi-simplicial objects, as a computational device for cohomology (likely with cup-product/multiplicative structure in view). It is only sketched here; the substantive content must lie on other pages.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: it parallels cochain-level models (E_∞ / commutative cochains) but adds nothing beyond known relative homological algebra on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a setup page: it fixes an exact structure, identifies relative projectives and injectives, and recalls the standard comparison theorem. It is an interesting window into Grothendieck's 1975–76 work on semi-simplicial ∂-perfect complexes, but contains no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'résolutions flasques K_* de k_*' — the second symbol appears to be k with a lower star (the constant coefficient system); fits context.
The insertion above line 3 reads 'i.e. Σ_1 = Σ ∩ P_1' (an inserted marginal phrase), not part of the list of L_i, Z_i, B_i, H_i.
'(qui donnent des un type algébrique' — likely 'qui donnent, en type algébrique(?), des méthodes de calcul remarquables'; reading uncertain.
